batchIdentityNotes.assessment: 1492 to 1500 Titicaca/Altiplano cultural outline. Aymara-speaking peoples comprised distinct polities, not one timeless kingdom. Narrative includes post-Inca and living phases.
1279 to 1492 broad outline extends far south into Atacama. Shared card explicitly discusses separate highland polities, Inca incorporation and territorial simplification. No outline repair performed.

1500 to 400 BCE coastal outline. Shared archaeological-culture narrative covers much earlier communities and later changing practices. Map endpoint 400 BCE is not supported as disappearance or end of artificial mummification; publicly qualified.

2000 to 1500 BCE Atacama coast outline, geographically broader than chinchoros. Same archaeological tradition; shared card covers UNESCO sites dated 5450 to 890 BCE and distinguishes dates of mummification from occupation. No precise state inferred.
1492 to 1500 Andahuaylas-region outline occurs after fifteenth-century Inca incorporation. Public opening qualifies this; traditional 1438 defeat not falsely given as an exact archaeological date.
1492 to 1500 outline extends to roughly 6°S, far north of Mantaro heartland. Public opening warns; Xauxa regional sites distinguished from a homogeneous Huanca kingdom. No geometry repair performed.

1492 to 1500 broad cross-Andean outline from roughly 21 to 32°S. Distinct Chilean archaeological tradition and Argentine local peoples distinguished, no unified empire. Contemporary evidence is dated; no goat husbandry projected before colonization.

1492 to 1500 small southern Bahia outline near Olivença. Public warning: modern local territorial footprint cannot stand for all historic Tupinambá or be projected literally to 1492. Wider featherwork history distinguished from specific later Olivença examples.
800 to 1000 broad Brazilian outline. Cultural-linguistic umbrella, not a single state; Tupi stock, Tupi-Guarani branch, Tupiniquim and Tupinambá distinguished. No extinction at 1000.

800 to 1400 MultiPolygon spans eastern Caribbean islands (approximately 12 to 18°N), not Lokono homeland. Card renamed to regional Arawakan-speaking context; language assignment to each archaeological site is explicitly unproven. North America region. NOT associated with lokono-arawak, whose decoded footprint is Guianas/Amazon-mouth region.
